value.rationale: Two canonical tree laws (uniform Catalan versus random-permutation BST) assign very different root-split tails. The exact root/cherry mixed dependency is negative in both but diverges at n^(3/2) under Catalan and converges to a finite constant under BST. A nonmonotone root-conditioned expectation reveals why simple balance-monotonicity reasoning fails. The structural comparison is useful when interpreting co-occurrence of local cherries and global root imbalance as tree-shape diagnostics, beyond reproducing any known marginal distribution.
